source.repro: products/jbrowse-web: node browser-tests/runner.ts --backend=all --skip-webgpu --swiftshader --gate-only --ci-gate --drift-report, once with the shader before the analytic band and once after, rebuilding @jbrowse/web between the two. Same machine, same run scope, 86 canvas2d-vs-webgl pairs both times.
source.notes: Canvas2D is the reference side: it rasterises `fillRect` at fractional y and has always antialiased a bar's top cut, so a GPU shader that computes the same coverage should move TOWARD it. Every pair that moved by more than 0.005% is listed and every one of them fell; none rose, and the summed drift over all 86 pairs went 5.09% to 4.75%. This is the WEBGL rung under swiftshader, so it also confirms the change on the backend the WebGPU captures do not cover. gc-skew is the negative-going bar, whose datum is its BOTTOM cut.
